policy.objective: Maximize sensitivity to true recursion and recursive lifecycle hazards. False positives are acceptable; false negatives are the primary failure.
policy.no_negative_filtering: Absence from typed evidence never removes or downgrades a classic candidate.
policy.uncertainty_rule: Unresolved feasibility defaults to precautionary_refactor, not false_positive_proven.
policy.suppression_expiry: A false-positive disposition is valid only for the recorded source SHA-256 and call sites; a source change reopens it.

manifest.audit_note: The audited source head identifies the final production bytes. Evidence-only manifest and audit-document commits do not invalidate source-bound dispositions when every recorded source SHA-256 remains equal.

The captured typed findings remain a positive union channel; classic analysis, source-SHA review, manual ownership review, compilation, and depth gates independently close the libdictenstein campaign.

The Loom fault model constructs only the explicit length-one fault-in topology used by its scenarios and bounds retry loops; it is not an input-shaped production traversal. FaultModelNode's custom Drop increments an optional counter and does not recurse; Rust's subsequent field drop remains bounded by the same length-one model topology.

ChildNode owns descendants through Vec. Manual iterative Clone, Debug, and Drop machines are implemented. Deep branching and chain tests pass at 100,000 levels; bounded property tests compare Clone/Debug with the recursive reference.

Raw in-memory child pointers are exclusive owned Box allocations hidden behind SwizzledPtr. Clone, Debug, and postorder Drop are explicit machines; chain and branching-spine gates pass at 100,000 levels, and Miri covers lifecycle plus clone-unwind ownership.
